claims.text: The specified AlCrFeNiSi feedstock is cobalt-free.
Conventionally processed AlCrFeNiSi can exhibit compositional heterogeneity.
Conventional LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi can produce residual stresses because of rapid thermal cycling and non-uniform solidification.
LPBF processing can produce defects whose prevalence depends on laser-processing conditions.
In-situ ultrasonic vibration with real-time sensor feedback can be integrated into LPBF during fabrication.
Ultrasonic vibration induces acoustic streaming in the molten pool.
Ultrasonic vibration induces cavitation in the molten pool.
Acoustic streaming and cavitation increase mass transport within the melt pool.
Ultrasonic agitation reduces melt-pool thermal gradients and improves mixing.
Enhanced melt-pool mass transport reduces local solute buildup and compositional segregation.
Ultrasonic-assisted solidification promotes more uniform grain nucleation and grain refinement.
Improved mixing and more uniform solidification alleviate residual-stress accumulation from rapid cooling.
Ultrasonic-assisted LPBF will reduce compositional-segregation indicators by approximately 50% relative to otherwise identical LPBF without ultrasound.
Ultrasonic-assisted LPBF will reduce defect density relative to otherwise identical LPBF without ultrasound.
Ultrasonic-assisted LPBF will lower residual stress relative to otherwise identical LPBF without ultrasound.
Ultrasonic-assisted LPBF will improve mechanical properties, including yield strength and ductility, by roughly 20–30%.
LPBF laser power, scan speed, and volumetric energy density influence defect formation, microstructure, and mechanical performance.
The proposed effects are expected to apply to cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi within standard LPBF energy-density and scan-speed ranges.
The magnitude of improvement depends on ultrasonic frequency, intensity, timing, and process tuning.
